title: Fast integration: UX voice and unit pricing hypotheses
content:
Goal: craft a short, testable set of developer-facing messages, quickstart hooks, and pricing microcopy that reduce time-to-first-success and lower hesitation during billing decisions. This doc is proposal + test plan (rough).

Context and assumptions:
- Audience: backend/frontend engineers and ML engineers evaluating an LLM inference provider for an integration that needs to be live in hours not weeks. Priorities: reliable latency, simple SDKs, visible costs during dev, straightforward free trial.
- Differentiation to lean on: predictable latency (SLOs), cost controls (batching, per-request caps), and the same API across hosted/dedicated/private. Not just model access — serving economics and operational predictability.
- Constraints: keep landing page copy short, but provide modular microcopy for SDK readme, pricing page, and onboarding emails.

1) Core developer-value statements (short, standalone lines to test)
- "Ship real LLM features in hours — one SDK, predictable latency, and built-in cost controls."
- "Start with free credits, keep latency tight — scale with reserved capacity when you need throughput."
- "Same API from prototype to production: hosted for speed, dedicated for SLAs, private for regulated workloads."

Voice notes: technical but friendly; assume developer understands tokens but not our backend. Use verbs like "ship, measure, control". Avoid marketing fluff like "AI-native" in the landing hero for dev audiences.

2) Quickstart hooks (for 30–60 minute activation)
- Headline: "Get a chat prototype running in 30 minutes"
- 3-step microflow (for README/landing secondary CTA):
  1) "Sign up and get $X in free credits"
  2) "Install our SDK and call chat.generate(sample_prompt) — change one line to swap models"
  3) "Enable real-time metrics and cost caps in Console — see per-token cost and latency breakdowns"
- Minimal code snippet (plain text for page):
  // Python (skeleton)
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
  resp = client.chat.create(model='open-vicuna-13b', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize my notes"}])
  print(resp.text)

Quickstart UX notes:
- Provide an immediate visible success: show a sample response in the UI after first API call, highlight tokens used and cost estimate.
- Inline "cost simulator" — let devs toggle model/length and see cost/latency estimates before calling.

3) Pricing-language drafts (microcopy for pricing and in-console nudges)
- Hero microcopy for pricing page:
  "Simple per-request and per-token pricing. Free trial credits. Predictable reserved capacity for high-throughput apps."
- Pricing bullets to test on page and in Console:
  - "Hosted API: pay per token + per-request base (useful for unpredictable usage)."
  - "Reserved/Dedicated: monthly commit for predictable throughput and lower per-token price."
  - "Private: license + infra fee for on-prem and VPC deployments."
- In-console badge copy (short):
  "Estimated cost: ~0.8¢ for this request (tokens: 184). Toggle quantized model to halve token compute costs."
- Pricing objections & suggested micro-responses (for sales & self-serve copy):
  - Q: "Why not cheaper like X cloud provider?" A: "We show you the math: per-token + per-request tradeoffs, automatic batching and caching reduce your unit spend — and you keep predictable latency."
  - Q: "Will cost spike in production?" A: "Use reserved capacity and burst controls — you can pin SLOs per route."

4) Landing/CTA variants to A/B test (short)
Variant A (developer-first): "Integrate LLMs — same API from prototype to SLA-backed production."
Variant B (metric-first): "Ship chat features with 50% fewer serving surprises. Start free."
Variant C (friction-minimizing): "From idea to working endpoint in one SDK install."

5) Competitive notes (quick scan for positioning copy)
- General cloud AI providers (CSPs): they sell infrastructure and model endpoints. Their pitch is flexibility and scale. Our counter: "We package serving optimizations and observability out-of-the-box — less ops, better unit economics for latency-sensitive apps."
- LLM API incumbents: strong brand and model access. Our counter: "Transparent unit economics + production-grade serving primitives (KV caches, fallback models, batching) that reduce real-world cost and variability."
- Self-hosted inference vendors: control is primary value. Our counter: "Private deployment option plus unified API across hosted/dedicated/private reduces migration risk — developers keep the same integration."

6) Objection response snippets for chat with devs (sales/dev-advocate playbook)
- "I need sub-100ms latency for short requests" -> "We recommend pinned model variants and single-request batching off. Our latency sled covers this on Dedicated plans; we include per-route latency budgets."
- "We care about cost predictability" -> "Try Reserved (monthly) with auto-burst and throttles; Console simulates monthly burn so you can forecast."

7) UX copy / Console micro-interactions (notes)
- Show a "cost preview" on the call modal. Add a small "optimize" link that suggests: smaller context window, quantized model, or enable KV cache for repeated prefixes.
- Add a "why this cost" tooltip breaking tokens vs compute price vs base request charge. Useful for PR and Slack screenshots in docs.

8) Suggested A/B experiments (MVP)
- Test 1: Hero copy A vs C (developer-first vs friction-minimizing) — measure sign-ups, time-to-first-success, and first-7d retention.
- Test 2: Pricing microcopy with and without explicit per-request base fee shown up front — measure upgrade intent and drop-off at payment screen.
- Test 3: Inline cost simulator vs no-simulator on quickstart page — measure number of API calls and mean token usage per account over first week.

9) TODOs / short-term action items
- Diego: add a lightweight cost estimator widget to /quickstart (JIRA-GTM-1987) — target: 1 week.
- Priya: draft one-pager for sales with objection snippets (due 2024-03-25).
- Jordan: wire two landing variants (A and C) to experiment framework; include event tags for time-to-first-success.
- Maya: iterate pricing page microcopy with legal & finance to confirm wording on "per-request base charge".

Open questions / things to validate with research:
- What free credit amount minimizes churn vs prompts experimentation? (benchmarks: $50 vs $200)
- Do devs prefer per-request base visible upfront, or hidden until billing? Which reduces cart abandonment?

Notes to self: keep the messaging utilitarian — help devs make the first call and understand the cost. Avoid vague performance claims; instead point to a short "how we measure" doc and sample latency percentiles for common models.

References / links to reuse:
- Quickstart repo with examples: github.com/redwood-inference/examples/quickstart-sdk
- Console mockups: CONFLUENCE-2456
- Experiment tracker ticket: JIRA-GTM-1987

End.
